result.title: Supervision-Adaptive Curriculum and Guarded Anti-Curriculum Learning for Dense Prediction
result.summary: Curriculum learning orders samples by difficulty, but difficulty alone does not establish supervision reliability for dense prediction. Easy samples can expose shortcuts, hard samples can be informative, and noisy or ambiguous samples can mislead training. Building on our conference method CurriSeg, we present PaceShift, a stabilize-then-challenge paradigm combining supervision-adaptive curriculum selection with guarded spectral post-training. A learning-dynamics view motivates separating supervision reliability from temporal update value and applying spectral challenges after stabilization. The first phase estimates reliability from available supervision, augmentation consistency, model disagreement, and prediction certainty. Temporal statistics guide sample weighting, while pixel-uncertainty weights reduce the early influence of uncertain regions. The second phase ranks predictions from multiple spectral views using supervision agreement, robustness, reference consistency, and penalties. A pairwise preference objective measured against the frozen Phase-I reference, together with an anchor, refines the prediction. The framework supports full, weak, semi-supervised, and model-derived supervision. Experiments across context-entangled content segmentation (CECS), broader dense-prediction tasks, and foundation-model and cross-modal adaptations show accuracy gains. Targeted diagnostics indicate improved pooled calibration and corruption robustness in the evaluated settings. PaceShift preserves the deployed architecture and adds no inference computation. Code will be publicly released.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PaceShift，一种面向密集预测的两阶段课程学习框架：先用监督一致性、增强一致性、模型分歧和预测确定性估计监督可靠性并加权样本，再以多光谱视图排序与冻结参考模型上的成对偏好目标做稳定后的强化训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「监督可靠性」与「时序更新价值」分离、并对像素级不确定区域降权的做法，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的训练信号设计与贡献分配提供核查线索，但论文本身不做多模态推理或 latent 状态研究。
